title: DevX Accelerator: SDK & Quickstart Cohort Playbook
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Create a repeatable cohort-based playbook (DevX Accelerator) that bundles SDKs, docs, and quickstarts into a tracked curriculum for new developer cohorts. The playbook will include templates for 1) a 1-hour quickstart flow, 2) a 3-day mini-project path, and 3) an integration checklist for Dedicated/Private customers. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-successful-call, increase 14-day retention of activated SDK users, and provide a clear handoff for solutions and success teams.
acceptance_criteria: Publish 3 quickstart templates (Node, Python, Go) with reproducible tests and CI
Create a cohort dashboard with activation and retention metrics in the Console analytics view
Document instructor notes and troubleshooting guide for Solutions team
Run a pilot cohort (n=25) and reach >= 40% 14-day retention after activation
Playbook approved by Developer Experience PMs and one Solutions rep
tasks: Draft quickstart flows and sample apps for Node/Python/Go
Add automated smoke tests that run against hosted API with test credentials
Wire minimal cohort metrics to Console (time-to-first-call, errors, retention)
Create Confluence playbook doc and instructor checklist
Coordinate pilot with Solutions to recruit 25 devs
Collect feedback and iterate on docs and SDK snippets
updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff — aligned on scope with Eng and Solutions. Agreed pilot size (25) and success metric (>=40% 14-day retention).
2026-03-11: Eng PR opened for Node quickstart sample app (github.com/redwood/sample-node-quickstart/pull/12). Added smoke test skeleton.
2026-03-12: Design review — simplified auth flow for first-hour quickstart. Decided to provide both API key and short-lived token example. UX feedback: reduce config friction.

2026-03-13: Console analytics contract drafted with ENG (ENG-1842). Need a small backend event for 'first_successful_call' and an aggregated retention view. Blocker: analytics schema change requires infra signoff.
risks: Analytics schema change may slip and delay dashboard availability
Hosted API rate limits could cause flakey smoke tests if pilot load spikes
Insufficient Solutions bandwidth to run pilot cohorts on schedule
SDK surface or breaking API changes could invalidate quickstart before pilot completes
next_steps: Unblock analytics schema: schedule meeting with infra on 2026-03-14
Complete Node/Python quickstarts and merge PRs by 2026-03-20
Prepare pilot recruitment email and Solutions runbook by 2026-03-22
Add smoke test CI and verify against staging environment
notes: This ticket intentionally ties SDK developer activation to Console observability so we can measure real downstream impact. We will treat the pilot as a learning experiment — prioritize removing friction over feature completeness for the first cohort.
